annotation_description: Chose to be on the draw with an aggressive low-curve hand (Marauding Mako, Iron-Shield Elf, Flamewake Phoenix, Bloodthorn Flail) that wants to maximize tempo. Going second loses a full turn of attacks and lets the opponent establish their board first.

Spending 2 mana to pump Burnout Bashtronaut by +1/+0 before combat is suboptimal. The player has a Mountain in hand they haven't played yet this turn, and Tersa Lightshatter costs 2R - by spending 2 mana on the pump, they cannot play their land and cast Tersa on turn 3 (they still can since they have 3 mountains, but the pump itself is questionable). More importantly, pumping a 1/1 menace to 2/1 before combat when the opponent has no creatures to block is wasteful - the opponent only has Blazemire Verge and no creatures. The extra 1 damage for 2 mana is very inefficient, and that mana could be better saved. However, since the opponent can't block anyway (no creatures), the pump does get through 1 extra damage. But at 20 life, this is a very low-value use of mana when the player should be developing their board - they could play their land and hold mana open, or simply save the mana.

Marauding Mako is a 1/1 that needs discard synergy to grow, while Bloodghast is a 2/1 with graveyard recursion via landfall. Bloodghast is a stronger standalone creature that provides more immediate pressure and is extremely resilient. Even if Mako could grow with Tersa Lightshatter discards next turn, Bloodghast's recursion and higher base power make it the superior turn 2 play.

annotation_description: Bloodghast costs {B}{B} and is already on the stack. Blazemire Verge provides one {B}, but Starting Town was tapped for {C} instead of paying 1 life for {B}. This results in only {B}{C} available, making it impossible to pay Bloodghast's casting cost, wasting the turn.

Tersa Lightshatter is a 3/3 haste creature that generates card advantage on attack (discards and draws on ETB, and exiles/plays cards from graveyard when attacking with 7+ cards in graveyard). It's a much more significant threat than Burnout Bashtronaut, which is currently a 1/1 menace that needs multiple turns and mana investment to become dangerous. Tersa is attacking for 3 damage per turn and providing card selection/advantage, while the Bashtronaut is only a 1/1. Using a premium removal spell like Bitter Triumph (which cost an additional card or 3 life) on the smaller, less impactful threat is a clear misallocation of resources.

Opponent has no creatures on the battlefield and no way to punish an all-out attack. Attacking with only Tersa Lightshatter leaves at least 2 damage on the table (1 from Hired Claw's attack + 1 from its Lizard attack trigger). Hired Claw has minimal defensive value since Bloodghast (the main threat from graveyard) can't block anyway.

Declined to activate Hired Claw's +1/+1 counter ability despite having spare mana ({1}{R} available from untapped lands) and nothing else to spend it on (hand is just two Mountains). The opponent lost life this turn (Tersa attacked), so the ability was activatable. A permanent +1/+1 counter on Hired Claw is pure value.

Declined to activate Rockface Village to give Hired Claw +1/+0, missing 1 extra damage when the opponent is at 9 life with no blockers. Every point of damage matters when racing to close out the game.

Declined to activate Hired Claw's +1/+1 counter ability with unused mana available, while the opponent is at 4 life. The permanent counter would make Hired Claw a 2/3, increasing damage output next turn to help close the game. An opponent lost life this turn, so the ability is activatable.

At 4 life facing lethal threats (Tersa Lightshatter 3/3 and Hired Claw will untap and attack), GPT5n Critic cast Monument to Endurance which provides no board presence or immediate survival value. The opponent's creatures will attack next turn and Monument does nothing to prevent that damage.
